# Question

**Does giving lots of high fives to teammates help sports teams win?** Kraus, Huang & Keltner (2010, *Emotion*) had two independent coder teams record celebratory teammate touch — high fives, fist bumps, chest bumps, hugs, huddles — for 294 players across all 30 NBA teams in the first two months of the 2008–09 season, then asked whether early-season touch predicted later performance.

## Data source

`win_pct` = real 2008–09 final standings (public record); per-player touch seconds were never published, so that column is a seeded (2026) reconstruction calibrated to the paper's 1.80 s mean and to Boston / L.A. being the touchiest teams. Results characterise the documented reconstruction, not a literal replication of the paper's statistics.

# Exploratory analysis

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| fig-cap: "Early-season celebratory touch vs final win percentage, 2008–09 NBA"
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(6.5, 4.2))
ax.scatter(df["touch_sec_per_player"], df["win_pct"], s=42,
           color="#4c72b0", alpha=0.85)
b, a = np.polyfit(df["touch_sec_per_player"], df["win_pct"], 1)
xs = np.linspace(df["touch_sec_per_player"].min(),
                 df["touch_sec_per_player"].max(), 50)
ax.plot(xs, a + b * xs, color="#c44e52")
ax.set_xlabel("Touch seconds per player (first 2 months)")
ax.set_ylabel("Final win percentage")
plt.tight_layout()
plt.show()
```

# Methods & results

Pearson correlation with Fisher-z CI (parametric), 100k-permutation randomization test, and 100k-resample percentile bootstrap.

| Quantity | Value |
|---|---|
| Teams (n) | 30 |
| Pearson r | **0.750** |
| R² | 0.562 |
| Parametric p (t) | 1.9e-06 |
| Randomization p (100k) | < 1e-05 |
| Fisher-z 95% CI | (0.534, 0.874) |
| Bootstrap 95% CI | (0.553, 0.896) |

# Decision

**Reject H₀: teams whose players touch more win more** — touch alone explains 56% of the variance in final win percentage. Direction matches the paper's cooperation interpretation; caveats: reconstructed touch column, and observational association (winning may also cause celebration).
